rows.pair: Home points vs away points (same game)
rows.note: Computed from the 174 official final scores. This is the number that decides whether a same-game side+total parlay is fairly priced as independent.
Out-of-sample residuals from the walk-forward run. The key input for pricing a same-game parlay that combines a side with a total. The interval includes zero, so independence is not rejected here.

rows.pair: Cover (vs our spread) AND over (vs our total), same game
rows.note: Joint hit rate 0.2290 vs 0.2377 under independence; dependence ratio 0.963. A ratio above 1.0 means the two legs land together more often than independent pricing assumes, which is how a book protects itself on same-game parlays.

rows.pair: Player A points vs player B points, same team, same game
rows.note: Needs per-player game logs. None were captured, so the cell is blank by policy rather than filled with an assumption.

rows.pair: Player points vs player rebounds, same player, same game
rows.note: Needs per-player game logs. Blank by policy.

rows.pair: Player points vs player assists, same player, same game
rows.note: Needs per-player game logs. Blank by policy.

rows.pair: Player points vs team total, same game
rows.note: Needs per-player game logs. Blank by policy.

rows.pair: Two legs in different games (cross-game parlay)
rows.note: Not measured on this sample. Independence is an ASSUMPTION used to price cross-game parlays, not a verified result. Treat as unverified.
